fields.features_heading: What a Lead Magnet Page Does After the Email
fields.features_subheading: A lead magnet landing page trades a free resource for a visitor's email. These six parts handle the trade and the follow-up.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the offer, get the page

Tell Emergent what you give away, who it is for, and what to ask each visitor. It builds the page, the form, and the signup table, then changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
The offer opens on the thank-you screen

Once the form is sent, the thank-you screen shows the checklist or the calculator result in place. Connect your email tool and the app also emails a copy to the visitor.
fields.feature_3:
A signup table in your own database

Each signup saves its email and answers to a database you own, with the link that sent it. Built apps connect to any tool with an API, and a new row can update a HubSpot contact.
fields.feature_4:
Follow-up that depends on the answers

Set a rule on any answer, such as a score below 60 or a team of 20 or more people. Each signup that matches can get its own email or post a Slack alert to whoever follows up on it.
fields.feature_5:
Signups by offer on one dashboard

The dashboard behind the page counts signups as they arrive, split by offer and by source. Run the checklist against the calculator for a month, then keep the stronger one.
fields.feature_6:
Publish on your domain, export later

Put the page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, where a developer can take it further.

fields.tab_content_1:
The checklist opens on the thank-you screen

Quillmark keeps the books for dental practices and gives away a 12-point year-end close checklist. Its form asks for an email and the number of dentists. The checklist opens on the thank-you screen, and a copy goes to the inbox. Halden Voss Dental signed up with 4 dentists, one of 412 downloads this month.
fields.tab_content_2:
15 hours a week, shown after the email

Plotwise sells scheduling software to landscaping companies. Its calculator asks how many crews you run and how many hours each crew spends on scheduling a week. Greyfield Lawn Care entered 6 crews at 2.5 hours each. The page held the result until the email field was filled, then showed 15 hours a week.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any score below 60 gets the rebrand workbook

Brackenfield Studio asks 8 questions about a small company's brand, one per screen, and scores the answers out of 100. Any score below 60 gets the rebrand workbook by email; a score of 60 or more gets a link to book a call. Rosalind Pryde of Crumbhouse Bakery scored 46, and the workbook went to her inbox.
fields.tab_content_4:
Wynne Alcott hears when a store spends $10,000 or more

Corviel Ads runs paid search for online stores and offers a free ad account audit. The form asks for the store's web address and monthly ad spend. A store spending $10,000 or more a month sends strategist Wynne Alcott a Slack message. Lattice Pet Supply asked for an audit with $14,000 a month in spend.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Lead Magnet Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to build a lead magnet landing page that hands over the offer and follows up based on each answer.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one problem the offer solves
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline as the result
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the email and one answer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Deliver the offer on screen first
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single problem for a single kind of visitor, such as closing the books at year end for a dental practice. A narrow offer is easier to write a headline for, and the people it brings in share a need you can follow up on.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the headline as what the visitor walks away with, not the format. "Close your year in 12 steps" says more than "Free checklist". Use the line under it for the format and the time it takes to use, such as a 10-minute read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the email and at most one answer that changes your follow-up, such as practice size or monthly ad spend. Cut any field you would not act on in the first week; each one is another reason to close the tab.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the offer on the thank-you screen and send a copy by email as a backup. A visitor who mistypes the address still leaves with the checklist, and the email copy gives them a way back to it next week.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the headline, the fields, and the delivery plan into one prompt. Emergent builds the page with its signup table. Prompt again for anything that reads wrong, such as the button label or the text on the thank-you screen.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test signup down every path
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up with a test address for each rule you set: one score below 60 and one above it, or one spend under $10,000 and one over. Check that each test gets the right email and that the Slack alert reaches the right person.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Connect your email tool and CRM, then publish on your domain. Share the link where the problem comes up, such as a post about year-end close, and watch signups by source for 2 weeks before you change the offer.

faq_plan.q: What is a lead magnet landing page?
faq_plan.a: A lead magnet landing page is a single page that offers something free, such as a year-end checklist, in exchange for a visitor's email address. It has one form and one goal, and each signup it collects is the start of your follow-up with that person.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a lead magnet landing page?
faq_plan.a: Choose one offer, write a headline that names its result, and ask for the email plus one answer that shapes your follow-up. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder, which builds the page and the signup table behind it from your prompt. Send a test signup down each path before you publish.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in lead magnet landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at what each page asks for and what it hands back. Check whether the headline names a result instead of a format, and whether the offer appears as soon as the form is sent. Then read the thank-you screen closely, because that is where the next step after the download is set up.

faq_plan.q: What offers make the best lead magnet landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Pick an offer that solves one problem your buyer has now and takes minutes to use, such as a checklist or a calculator. Keep longer formats for buyers who want depth: an ebook landing page fits that case, with the table of contents shown so readers know what they are signing up for.

faq_plan.q: What do gated content landing page examples leave ungated?
faq_plan.a: The strong ones leave the description of the offer ungated: the headline, what it covers, and a preview such as the first checklist item or a sample result. Gate only the full resource. A visitor who can see what they will get has a reason to type an email, while a page that hides everything asks for trust it has not earned.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields should a lead magnet landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Start with two: the email and one answer you will act on, such as company size. Leave the name out unless your first email uses it. If you test a third field, run it for a few weeks and compare signups you would follow up on, not raw totals. Pages Emergent builds store each answer as its own column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How is a lead magnet landing page different from a regular signup page?
faq_plan.a: A lead magnet page trades a specific resource for the email, while a plain signup page asks for it on the promise of updates. A lead generation landing page goes further and can collect demo or quote requests, where the visitor wants a conversation instead of a download.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up with people who sign up on a lead magnet landing page?
faq_plan.a: Send the first email the same day and name the offer they took in the subject line. Split later emails by the extra answer on the form. For signups worth a personal reply, Emergent can build an email or in-app alert to the person who owns that follow-up.

faq_plan.q: How do I know if my lead magnet landing page is working?
faq_plan.a: Divide signups by visitors for the signup rate, and track it by source so one strong channel does not hide a weak one. Then look further down: how many signups opened the follow-up email or booked a call within 30 days. Change one thing at a time, such as the headline, and compare the next month.

faq_plan.q: Can one lead magnet landing page work for different audiences?
faq_plan.a: It can when the offer stays the same; build a separate page when the offer changes with the reader. A home value estimate belongs on a real estate landing page, while a year-end close checklist belongs on a bookkeeping firm's page. Emergent builds each version from a prompt, and a new prompt changes the offer and the fields for the next audience.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example galleries (Instapage, Swipe Pages, Dribbble, Pinterest, Webflow) and lead magnet idea lists (MailerLite, Zendesk); each shows the page but not what happens after the email is typed in. This page shows four lead magnet landing pages working by offer type: a checklist that opens on the thank-you screen, a calculator that shows its result after the email, an 8-question score that sends a different follow-up by result, and an audit request that alerts a strategist on big accounts. The FAQ answers what searchers ask about examples, gated content, offer choice, form length and delivery. Squeeze, ebook, whitepaper and lead generation pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
